shadows.purpose: A ticket at rest in the rail.

shadows.purpose: A stock-up board flash card at rest.

shadows.name: flash-lead-entry

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: The single easing for every transition in the system.

motion.name: step
motion.purpose: Stagger unit, multiplied by a per-row index capped at 14.

motion.name: seat
motion.purpose: A slot seats into the rail from translateX(-20px) rotate(-1.5deg).

motion.name: rise-proud
motion.purpose: The cheaper ticket rises only after both are seated, so the comparison resolves visibly.

motion.name: tag-turn
motion.purpose: The special flash turns over onto the ticket from rotate(-16deg) opacity 0.

motion.name: stamp-strike
motion.purpose: The rarity stamp is struck on from scale(1.5) opacity 0.

motion.name: flash-lead-stamp
motion.purpose: Focal moment: the board's lead card is stamped down from scale(1.07) translateY(-10px).

motion.name: flash-rest-settle
motion.purpose: The board's two secondary cards settle from translateY(-14px).

motion.name: hover-lift
motion.purpose: Pointer states: ticket 14px (17px if proud), flash 3px.

motion.name: sign-light
motion.purpose: Bay signs light from rail grey to sign black as the aisle is walked, where scroll-linked animation is supported.

notes: The build declares no width media queries. Responsive behaviour is entirely intrinsic: the slot caps at 22rem and the column at 46rem, so a wide viewport gains margin rather than ticket width.

Conditional rules in the build: @supports not (grid-template-rows:subgrid) falls back to flex with margin-top:auto on the price; @supports not (color-mix()) drops the stamp's tinted offset to a solid one; @supports (animation-timeline:view()) gates the bay-sign lighting.
There is no JavaScript on the page. Every state is server-rendered by render.py and every effect is CSS out of @starting-style inside prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference.

narrative.overview:
This is one surface pretending to be furniture. The page is a grey supermarket aisle; each tracked product is a pair of white die-cut price tickets seated side by side in a grey plastic rail, one ticket per chain, and each bay of the list is introduced by a black overhead bay sign. Everything is printed: square corners everywhere, no rounded UI, no gradients, no imagery, and no icons of any kind. Density is high and unapologetic, because the whole week's decision has to survive one phone screen in one hand.

The only element that is not shop signage is the rarity stamp: a violet double-ruled strike saying whether this price is genuinely unusual. It is the app's own voice, inked in a hue that belongs to neither chain and is not the focus ring's blue, and it is the reason the page exists rather than a shelf photo.

Chain identity is colour, never a logo: Woolworths green and Coles red arrive as a 5px printed top edge on every slot. Because red is a chain's name here, red can never also mean "discount" — the special vocabulary is built from the chains' own yellow flash instead. The page carries no JavaScript; every state and every motion is CSS, and the finished, readable state is the element's real state.
keyCharacteristics: Printed-ticket material: white card on grey aisle, square corners, hairline rules
Heavy condensed grotesque throughout, pack price at ticket scale
Chain colour as the only identity mark, no logos
Yellow flash for specials, violet stamp for rarity, red only for Coles or a dead pin
Motion is stagger-and-seat only, out of @starting-style, never required to read the page

rules.name: The Reserved Red Rule
rules.body: Red means Coles, or a dead pin. It never encodes discount depth, saving size, or urgency. A half-price Woolworths line is a red burst on yellow card, never a red card, because a red Woolworths ticket would arrive wearing its rival's colour.

rules.name: The Printed Card Rule
rules.body: Dark mode darkens the aisle, the rail, the bay sign and the body ink only. The ticket stays white with its own near-black ink, because printed card does not change colour under different light.

rules.name: The Two Inks Rule
rules.body: The stamp's violet and the focus ring's blue are separate inks and stay separate. The stamp is content; the ring is the browser talking.

rules.name: The No Logo Rule
rules.body: Chain identity is carried by colour alone. No retailer logo, wordmark or brand asset appears on any surface.

rules.name: The Pack Price Leads Rule
rules.body: On every ticket the pack price is the largest type in the slot and the unit price sits beneath it, small, as the tiebreaker. Price per unit is never promoted to the headline; it is the number that decides but not the number that is recognised.

rules.name: The Condensed Scan Rule
rules.body: Anything scanned (chain, product, price, sign, tag, stamp) is uppercase Barlow Condensed. Anything read as prose is upright Barlow, mixed case. There is no third voice.

rules.name: The One Figure Style Rule
rules.body: font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums is set on the document, so two prices in a pair align digit for digit.

rules.name: The Shared Rows Rule
rules.body: A pair's two slots inherit the same four subgrid rows. Never give one slot of a pair its own internal row structure; the compared prices must sit on a shared baseline.

rules.name: The Capped Slot Rule
rules.body: Widening the viewport adds margin, never ticket width. A ticket's maximum is 22rem.

rules.name: The Proud Means Cheaper Rule
rules.body: Vertical lift inside a pair is reserved for the cheaper unit price. Nothing else in the rail may stand proud, so height stays readable as a verdict.

rules.name: The Print Depth Rule
rules.body: Shadows are short, dark and downward — card on rail. No glow, no coloured shadow, no blur above 15px.

rules.name: The Missing Is Not Broken Rule
rules.body: A chain that does not stock a line is a grey hatched slot. A pin that no longer resolves is a red fault card. A read that failed this run is a grey fault card. Only the middle one is the reader's job, and only the middle one may be red.

rules.name: The Layered Motion Rule
rules.body: All seven effects are CSS transitions out of @starting-style, inside prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference, timed on one stagger step (38ms, multiplied by a per-row index capped at 14) and one easing (cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1)). The seated state is the element's real state, so a browser that runs none of it shows the finished shop.

dos: Do lead every price slot with the pack price at display scale (800, 2.9rem) and set the unit price small beneath it as the tiebreaker.
Do identify a chain with colour and colour only, as the 5px top edge of the slot.
Do express a special in the chains' yellow flash vocabulary: yellow card, yellow tag, burst red for half price only.
Do keep the ticket white in dark mode and darken only aisle, rail, sign and body ink.
Do give both slots of a pair the same four subgrid rows and the same 10.6rem minimum, so the two prices share a baseline.
Do reserve vertical lift inside a pair for the cheaper unit price.
Do ship any new effect as a transition out of @starting-style under prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference, on the existing 38ms step and easing.
Do self-host any new face through docs/fonts/faces.css.
donts: Don't use red to mean discount, saving, or urgency. Red is Coles, or a dead pin.
Don't place a retailer logo, wordmark or brand asset anywhere.
Don't paint a transient read failure red; it is grey, because red means the reader has work to do.
Don't round a corner. Nothing in this system carries a radius.
Don't add JavaScript to the page, or make any content reachable only after a transition runs.
Don't stretch a ticket past 22rem on a wide screen; add margin instead.
Don't introduce a third type voice or a fourth accent ink. Violet is the stamp, blue is the focus ring, yellow is the special.
Don't promote price per unit to the headline, and don't fall back to a comparison-dashboard card grid.
